cards.explanation: The answer is to see the land given to Israel. The LORD tells Moses, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) The land is already given, and Moses gets the view. I bet that climb had him huffing, but what a front-row seat.

The answer is False, and it's a tender one, friends. God doesn't say Moses will lead Israel into the land. He says, "After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) Moses gets to see it, and he is gathered to his people.

The answer is Aaron. God says Moses will be gathered to his people "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) The next verse says why, and it names both brothers, because both of them rebelled against God's command at the waters. So the brothers' stories line up right to the end.

The answer is True, and God says it straight. He tells Moses, "…both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters." (Numbers 27:14) Both of them, Moses and Aaron. The text doesn't soften it, so I won't either.

The answer is a man to lead the congregation, friends. Moses has just heard he'll be gathered to his people, and he doesn't start with himself. He asks the LORD to "…appoint a man over the congregation…" (Numbers 27:16) I think that's a man thinking about the people he's leaving behind. Even with that news, his mind is on them.

The answer is sheep without a shepherd. Moses asks for a leader so that "…the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) Sheep with no shepherd are like a batch of cookies with nobody watching the timer. Nobody is looking out for them, and that's how things end up burnt. Jesus uses this same picture when He sees the crowds and has compassion on them. (Matthew 9:36)
The answer is Spirit. God calls Joshua son of Nun "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) Look at what God points to, friends. He doesn't read out a résumé. He names who is in the man.

The answer is to lay his hands on him. God says, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) It's a simple act, and Moses does it when the time comes. (Numbers 27:23)

The answer is False, friends. God wants it out in the open. Joshua is to "…stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation…" and be commissioned "…in their sight…" (Numbers 27:19) That's the opposite of private.

The answer is so the congregation will obey him. God says, "Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) Notice it says some of Moses' authority, and the point is that the people will follow him. A new leader with nothing behind him gets a lot of shrugs, and this one gets backing in front of everybody.

The answer is counsel. God says Eleazar the priest "…will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) Eleazar does the seeking, friends, and he does it for Joshua before the LORD.

The answer is True. The text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) Then it shows him doing it. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation. Now THAT is how you follow a recipe, bakers. No skipped steps.
